subject: design-technology
title: CAD Basics
welcome_lead: Designing on a computer with software like SketchUp or Tinkercad.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: CAD, CAM, 3D modelling basics.
final_note: CAD lets you test ideas before cutting any material.

walkthroughs.body_html: CAD (Computer Aided Design) means designing on a computer. Tinkercad, SketchUp and Fusion 360 are popular CAD tools. You can spin, slice and test the design.
CAM takes a CAD file and tells a machine how to make it. A CNC router cuts wood, a 3D printer builds up plastic, a laser cutter slices through sheet material.
For 3D printing, save your CAD model as an STL file. The printer software slices it into layers and prints each one in order — usually plastic plastic filament.
